chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan, and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

If you catch the game while you are in Ihram inside the Haram, the ransom is doubled upon you; and if you catch it while you are Halal (not in Ihram) inside the Haram, its price is single; and if you catch it while you are in Ihram in the Hil (unrestricted area), then upon you is only one ransom.

key_terms.حَرَام: In the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in hunting penalty for a pilgrim in Ihram inside Mecca versus outside Mecca?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between the sanctity of the location and the state of Ihram, establishing that the severity of the penalty (fidyah) is determined by the intersection of these two factors. It specifically notes that hunting within the Haram boundaries while in Ihram incurs a double penalty, reflecting the compounded sanctity of the place and the ritual state, whereas hunting in the open country (Hil) while in Ihram incurs only a single penalty. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise legal categorization in ritual obligations.
